answer: Random jury sampling at the sparrow: any verdict requires 9 jurors drawn without replacement from the staked identity pool. The karst of sybil farming erodes fast — an attacker holding k fraction of identities wins a full jury only k^9 of the time. That spiral is brutal: at 30% control, odds collapse to 0.002%, so buying identities to swing verdicts costs more than honest stake could ever return. Conclusion: superlinear jury odds make vote-buying economically self-defeating.
